Reduced cell-surface availability is a supported explanation for the R252H taurocholate-uptake defect in the tested cells.
S267F changes NTCP transport in a substrate-dependent way, not simply by eliminating all transporter activity or surface abundance.
The 2015 taurocholate uptake result is explained by loss of NTCP sodium-contacting side-chain residue identities in SLC10A4.
Differences at mapped NTCP sites are sufficient to explain an absence of NTCP-like bile-acid transport by human SLC10A7.
Detectable preS1 binding alone establishes productive viral infection in the tested system.

NTCP S267F has opposite effects on two assayed substrates
